definitions.explanation: An arrangement to record purchases and settle the total later rather than paying each time; by extension, the negative consequences of past actions that eventually come due.

examples.english: I have an unpaid tab at the shop.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い⟦ころ→〜ころ：03091_koro⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ツケ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧になって⟦{回|まわ}って→回る：01150_mawaru⟧きた。
examples.english: The price of overdoing it when I was young has finally caught up with me.

notes:
Usually written in katakana as ツケ (also ⟦{付|つ}け→付く：01960_tsuku⟧). Refers to buying now and paying later on a running account, a practice once common at neighborhood bars and shops.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ツケ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧: to buy on credit / on a tab
- ツケ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧たまる: for an unpaid tab to build up
- ツケ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{払|はら}う→払う：00535_harau⟧: to settle the tab
- ツケ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{回|まわ}って→回る：01150_mawaru⟧くる: for past excesses to catch up with one

USAGE:
The figurative sense — the ⟦{代償|だいしょう}→代償：11432_daishou⟧ (price) of earlier carelessness coming due — is very common, especially in ツケ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{回|まわ}って→回る：01150_mawaru⟧くる.
